paper.title: Authentication Mechanism Comparison
paper.context: Compare implementation choices against the stated contracts. Assume current server-side data is authoritative unless the scenario says otherwise.

objectives.choose-evidence: Choose evidence that matches the caller and trust boundary.
objectives.plan-withdrawal: Compare request-time cancellation and availability guarantees.
objectives.place-state: Distinguish issuance dependencies from the serving path.
objectives.protect-evidence: Place each secret and trust artifact at the appropriate boundary.
objectives.make-decision: Choose an authentication design from operational requirements.

questions.prompt: A browser sends a valid-looking session reference after the server removes its record. What should the application restore?

choices.beta: No authenticated identity from that reference
choices.gamma: The identity in the cookie name
choices.delta: A read-only version of the old principal

questions.prompt: A partner uses one API key across all of its jobs. What can successful key verification establish?

choices.beta: That it has permission for every endpoint
choices.delta: That the network source is the partner’s private subnet

questions.prompt: A resource server uses uncached introspection. Its authority returns a valid response with active=false. What is justified?

choices.delta: Allow from the caller’s claimed scope

questions.prompt: A payments API locally verifies a JWT signed by its configured issuer. The token names inventory as its only audience. What should happen?

choices.alpha: Accept since both APIs trust the issuer
choices.beta: Check the subject name and accept if it exists
choices.gamma: Rewrite the audience from the request host
choices.delta: Reject the token for this API

questions.prompt: The gateway terminates mTLS. Application ingress can also be reached independently of the gateway. What closes the identity handoff gap?

choices.alpha: Let the application trust the identity header on any HTTPS connection
choices.beta: Authenticate and constrain the gateway-to-app channel and prevent bypass
choices.gamma: Treat the certificate subject as a universal permission
choices.delta: Share the gateway’s private key with the app

questions.prompt: New OAuth issuance is unavailable, but an API has an unexpired JWT and cached trusted keys. What follows in the stated profile?

choices.alpha: An existing request can still be evaluated locally
choices.beta: Every existing credential immediately becomes invalid
choices.gamma: Existing credentials gain more lifetime automatically
choices.delta: The API should bootstrap a new trust key from the header

questions.prompt: An API caches active introspection results for 60 seconds. Product promises no use more than 10 seconds after withdrawal. Which design addresses the conflict?

choices.gamma: Bound stale acceptance within 10 seconds including propagation, and fail closed beyond it

questions.prompt: A report request fans out to four downstream APIs. Each does one remote introspection without caching. What does replacing those checks with local JWT verification change?

choices.beta: It makes issuance independent of the identity platform
choices.delta: It removes four remote verdict reads per fan-out under the stated model

questions.prompt: An integration key was added to a compiled browser application. What is the right incident response?

choices.alpha: Withdraw and replace it, then move use behind a server or managed workload
choices.beta: Move it from JavaScript to a frontend environment variable
choices.delta: Encrypt it with another key embedded in the same bundle

questions.prompt: A workforce browser needs user presence. A scheduler runs unattended and must be independently revocable. How should credentials be assigned?

choices.alpha: Give the scheduler a copy of an employee’s browser cookie
choices.beta: Use separate human and workload principals with separate lifecycles
choices.gamma: Give both a shared global partner secret
choices.delta: Require an employee’s login for each scheduled retry

questions.prompt: Read the fixture. With a withdrawn grant and unreachable authority, which outcome follows for allows(false, false, true, 8, 9)?

choices.alpha: Denied because the grant is withdrawn
choices.beta: Denied because the authority is offline
choices.gamma: Allowed by this fixture before expiry, with withdrawal undetected

questions.prompt: Design authentication for a same-origin staff console, a managed billing worker and read APIs that must withhold data within ten seconds of withdrawal. Explain the caller boundaries, credential placement, outage behavior and what you would test before release.

feedback.alpha: Display state does not prove a current login.
feedback.beta: The reference needs a matching current record.
feedback.gamma: The name chooses the cookie field, not an account.
feedback.delta: Invalidation removes the basis for restoring that principal.

session-reference.reason: Check the session record before constructing the principal.

feedback.alpha: The credential is shared across jobs and carries no verified human evidence.
feedback.beta: Authorization still depends on the key’s registered permissions.
feedback.gamma: Verification binds the request to the registered key identity.
feedback.delta: The key does not prove network location.

key-attribution.reason: Record a key identifier for attribution and separately verify the action scope.

feedback.alpha: The trusted authority says the presented token is inactive.
feedback.beta: The contract does not support local verification of this opaque handle.
feedback.gamma: TLS authenticates the connection peer under its configuration and says nothing about token activity.
feedback.delta: Authorization cannot rest on a claimed scope.

opaque-record.reason: Distinguish an inactive response from an unavailable authority in internal diagnostics.

feedback.alpha: Shared issuer trust does not imply shared audiences.
feedback.beta: An existing subject does not repair the profile mismatch.
feedback.gamma: The request host cannot alter verified token claims.
feedback.delta: A verified token still needs the intended audience.

strict-local.reason: Unit-test a valid signature with a wrong audience.

feedback.alpha: TLS alone does not identify the trusted gateway as sender.
feedback.beta: The app receives mapped identity only from the verified boundary.
feedback.gamma: Certificate identity is distinct from application authorization.
feedback.delta: Sharing a private key does not establish a trusted assertion channel.

gateway-proof.reason: Enforce and test the trust boundary where certificate verification terminates.

feedback.alpha: Issuance is separate from the local serving decision.
feedback.beta: No revocation or expiry signal is implied by an outage.
feedback.gamma: The profile’s time bounds still hold.

issuer-outage.reason: Measure issuance and serving availability separately.

feedback.alpha: That still exceeds the stated maximum.
feedback.beta: A secure connection does not reduce verdict age.
feedback.gamma: The guarantee concerns the total time an old active decision can be used.
feedback.delta: The API is accepting a cached active access-token verdict.

cached-cancellation.reason: Include propagation and failure behavior in the cancellation budget.

feedback.alpha: Each API must still authorize its own action.
feedback.gamma: Signature and claim checks still require work.
feedback.delta: Existing checks become local if trusted keys are available.

fanout-load.reason: Measure both request-path latency and key distribution and rotation costs.

feedback.alpha: The distributed key cannot remain confidential.
feedback.beta: Values shipped to the browser remain accessible.
feedback.gamma: The fact that the secret was distributed is unchanged.
feedback.delta: The client has both the ciphertext and the means to recover it.

storage-boundary.reason: Rotate exposed credentials and stop shipping private evidence in public assets.

feedback.beta: The contracts differ in who acts and how access is cancelled.
feedback.gamma: A shared secret erases per-actor accountability and cancellation.
feedback.delta: It fails the unattended execution contract.

caller-split.reason: Separate audit and permissions according to the acting principal.

feedback.alpha: This decision can consult revocation only on a required live path.
feedback.beta: The live lookup branch is disabled.
feedback.gamma: The time check passes and local-only policy skips the authority.

offline-policy.reason: Use a live or otherwise current check when withdrawal must take effect before token expiry.

migration-record.reason: Use server-side sessions for the staff UI with scoped cookies and CSRF protection where appropriate. Give the worker a separate scoped identity, with mTLS if the gateway must verify private-key possession, and protect the key in its managed environment. For a read API use online authoritative verification or another current-state design whose end-to-end staleness can be bounded to ten seconds, including propagation and failure. Withhold protected data once that bound cannot be established. Test same-origin handling, worker identity binding, the exact cancellation boundary and upstream outage.
rubric: Distinguish the human and workload identities.
Justify evidence and storage for each caller.
Explain certificate verification and trusted handoff if selecting mTLS.
Account for propagation, caching and outages in the cancellation budget.
Specify before-boundary, at-boundary and outage checks.
